objective.value: Establish a general biosynthetic platform for producing structurally diverse C3-C5 diols (especially branched-chain 1,n-diols) in E. coli by combining an oxidative pathway (amino-acid hydroxylase) with a reductive pathway (deaminase -> decarboxylase -> aldehyde reductase) for formation of the two hydroxyl groups, and demonstrate the route by synthesizing 10 diols and optimizing IPDO production.
objective.notes: Subject = current_article. Six of ten diols (IPDO, 2-M-1,3-BDO, 2-M-1,4-BDO, MPO, 2-E-1,3-PDO, 1,4-PTD) claimed as first biological synthesis (paper_claim level, 'To our knowledge' qualifier in results_p014).

hypothesis.value: Combining an oxidative hydroxyl-group formation (alpha-KG-coupled amino-acid hydroxylation, strongly exergonic, no extra NAD(P)H/ATP) with a reductive hydroxyl-group formation (deamination/decarboxylation/reduction) in a thermodynamically favorable reaction order overcomes the thermodynamic and energetic drawbacks of exclusively reductive diol pathways; reaction order (hydroxylation first) and hydroxylase catalytic efficiency determine pathway performance.
hypothesis.notes: Thermodynamic rationale (Delta_rG -100 to -120 kcal/mol for hydroxylation step) is author interpretation supported by group-contribution calculations (Fig. 4); FBA theoretical yield 0.628 mol IPDO/mol glucose is model output, not measured.

strain.value: Production/expression host: Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) (strains DL01-DL08, DL01-R12, DL01-R34, DL01-R4, IP01-IP11). Cloning host: E. coli Top10. Directed-evolution selection host: E. coli BL21 ΔsucAΔaceAΔputA (DE3)(pLysS), paper label Δ3A (gift from B. Bühler group, ref 35). Enzyme gene donor strains (not experimental hosts): Methylobacillus flagellatus KT (mfl), Proteus vulgaris (aad_vul), Lactobacillus lactis (kdc), E. coli W3110 (yqhD, leuA^fbrBCD), Pantoea ananatis AJ13355 (hilA, hilB), Streptomyces DSM 40835 (griE), Agrobacterium vitis (avi), Bordetella petrii (bpe), Bacillus thuringiensis (ido), Gluconobacter oxydans (gox), Zymomonas mobilis (pdc), Saccharomyces cerevisiae (thi3), Bacillus subtilis (alsS).
strain.notes: Exact strain/plasmid genotype list deferred to Supplementary Data 1 (requires_supplement for full plasmid inventory). 'wild type' (MFL_wt) refers to unmutated MFL enzyme, not a strain.

genotype.value: DL01: BL21(DE3) + pET28a-mfl + pZA-aad_vul-kdc-yqhD (pZA-aky). DL02/DL03: hilA or hilB replacing mfl plus aad_vul, kdc, yqhD. DL04: griE replacing mfl. outcomes.value: 10 C3-C5 diols produced (titers 48 h): MPO 18.5 mg/L (from valine), IPDO 230.5 mg/L (leucine), 1,3-BDO 8.7 mg/L (norvaline), 1,3-PTD 4.2 mg/L (norleucine) via DL01; 2-E-1,3-PDO 145.2 mg/L (DL02) and 2-M-1,3-BDO 12.1 mg/L (DL03) from isoleucine; 2-M-1,4-BDO 276.4 mg/L, 1,4-BDO 7.8 mg/L, 1,4-PTD 11.9 mg/L via DL04; 1,3-PDO 6.7 mg/L (DL06) and 29.1 mg/L (DL08); DL05/DL07 (PDC) produced no 1,3-PDO. Reaction order: R1 (374.1 mg/L IPDO from 5 mM 4OH-Leu) >> R3 (19.2 mg/L from 5 mM KIC); R2, R4, R5, R6 excluded. Precursor engineering: IP08 20.5, IP09 55.7, IP10 77.6 mg/L IPDO without leucine feeding; valine byproduct 7.08 mg/L (IP09) reduced to 5.43 mg/L (IP10). Directed evolution: MFL_m1 (H138Q) 1.9-fold and MFL_m2 (S98G) 1.5-fold WT activity on leucine; IP11 reached 0.31 g/L IPDO (1.3-2.0x IP10 over 24-96 h). Second library: MFL_Hm1 (D57V/K235E) 2.5-fold WT. FBA theoretical IPDO yield 0.628 mol/mol glucose.
outcomes.notes: All titers are direct observations from shake-flask cultures; fold improvements of mutant enzymes measured in vitro. Claim 'six diols not biologically synthesized before' is authors' novelty claim ('To our knowledge'). Mechanistic explanation for DL05/DL07 failure (PDC inhibition) is explicitly speculative ('One possible interpretation').

experiments.purpose: Demonstrate in vivo function of the 4-enzyme platform pathway (hydroxylase/deaminase/decarboxylase/reductase) for 10 diols from 6 amino-acid substrates
experiments.intervention: Co-expression of MFL (pET28a) + AADvul/KDC/YqhD (pZA-aky) = DL01; variants DL02 (hilA), DL03 (hilB), DL04 (griE), DL05-DL08 (avi/bpe x pdc/kdc for 1,3-PDO)
experiments.conditions: FM-II + 25 mM respective amino acid, 37 °C, 200 rpm, 48 h, 1 mM IPTG induction at OD 0.4-0.6
experiments.control: Not explicitly reported in main text (requires_supplement)
experiments.readout: GC-FID diol titer; GC-MS identity confirmation
experiments.outcome: 9 of 10 target diols produced from BCAA/threonine substrates (titers 4.2-276.4 mg/L); DL05/DL07 with PDC produced no 1,3-PDO
experiments.subject: current_article

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: authors designed and assembled a novel heterologous 4-enzyme cascade (new engineering action, done in this paper, establishing the platform on which all later optimization depends).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Pathway parsing/design: assembling hydroxylase->deaminase->decarboxylase->reductase route from amino acids to diols.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Prior diol pathways rely exclusively on reductive OH formation requiring extra ATP and 4 NAD(P)H with low driving force (Delta_rG ~ -5 to -1 kcal/mol) and toxic aldehyde intermediates; oxidative hydroxylation coupled to alpha-KG->succinate is strongly exergonic (-100 to -120 kcal/mol).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: The thermodynamic driving-force argument is based on group-contribution estimates and literature values (predictive, requires experimental confirmation); the in vivo function itself was then experimentally verified (hard) in this same step.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly gives a thermodynamic mechanism: coupling hydroxylation to alpha-KG oxidation provides large driving force, avoids ATP/NAD(P)H burden, and deamination+decarboxylation push the final reduction; intermediates' toxicity considerations also stated.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When designing synthetic pathways to diols (or molecules with multiple hydroxyl groups) in E. coli, apply a mixed oxidative+reductive OH-formation strategy ordered hydroxylation>deamination>decarboxylation>reduction, because alpha-KG-coupled oxidative hydroxylation supplies a large thermodynamic driving force without extra ATP/NAD(P)H while downstream deamination/decarboxylation pull the thermodynamically weaker final reduction.
alternatives_considered: Purely reductive pathways (as in prior 1,4-BDO/1,3-BDO routes) - rejected due to ATP cost, low driving force, and aldehyde toxicity

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: deliberate choice of position-selective hydroxylases to determine which carbon is hydroxylated, thereby defining product structure.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Rate-limiting/key enzyme selection: hydroxylase identity sets hydroxylation position (C-4 vs C-5) and thus diol structure.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Literature-reported position selectivity of hydroxylases from different species (C-4: MFL/AVI/IDO/GOX/BPE; C-5: GriE; isoleucine C4-1/C4-2: HilA/HilB).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Subsequent titers confirmed in vivo function; selection rationale itself rests on literature-characterized substrate spectra (previously measured).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Choices explicitly based on prior characterizations (refs 15, 17, 24); GriE additionally chosen for broad substrate spectrum and available crystal structure.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When producing position-defined diols from amino acids in E. coli, apply hydroxylase selection by reported regioselectivity (C-4 vs C-5 vs substrate-specific), because hydroxylase choice alone determines the carbon position of the oxidative OH group and hence product identity from the same amino-acid precursor.
alternatives_considered: AVIDO and IDO as C-5 hydroxylases - rejected for narrower substrate spectra than GriE

experiments.purpose: Produce 1,3-PDO by extending threonine catabolism (threonine hydroxylase AVI/BPE + endogenous IlvA deaminase + KDC/PDC + YqhD)
experiments.intervention: First iteration: AVI or BPE assembled with KDC or PDC relying on endogenous IlvA (4 strains); second iteration: overexpression of hydroxylase + decarboxylase + YqhD to enforce hydroxylation-first order (DL05-DL08)
experiments.conditions: FM-II + 25 mM threonine, 48 h shake flask
experiments.control: Comparison among the four enzyme combinations; no empty-vector control reported
experiments.readout: GC-FID 1,3-PDO titer; in vitro threonine-deaminase assay on 4-hydroxy-threonine (Suppl. Fig. 14)
experiments.analysis: titer comparison; in vitro activity confirmation
experiments.outcome: First iteration: no 1,3-PDO from any of 4 strains. After overexpression: DL06 6.7 mg/L, DL08 29.1 mg/L (KDC); DL05/DL07 (PDC) still zero.
experiments.subject: current_article

interventions_ddr.name: Overexpression to enforce hydroxylation-first order in 1,3-PDO pathway

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: failure of first construct set triggered a new construct design (overexpression of AVI/BPE + KDC/PDC + YqhD) that changed pathway outcome and informed the reaction-order principle used later.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Expression balancing to resolve kinetic mismatch between competing enzymes.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: All four initial strains produced zero 1,3-PDO; authors attribute this to endogenous IlvA outcompeting hydroxylases for threonine because IlvA kcat is ~16,000-fold higher than AVI/BPE.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Zero-titer observation is measured; the kcat comparison draws on reported kinetic parameters (measured in cited studies).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper gives explicit kinetic-competition mechanism (IlvA vs hydroxylase kcat mismatch, ~16,000-fold) as the reason for overexpressing the hydroxylase so hydroxylation precedes deamination.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a pathway intermediate is also substrate of a much faster endogenous enzyme (here threonine vs IlvA in E. coli 1,3-PDO production), apply overexpression of the desired first-step enzyme so the intended reaction precedes the competing native reaction, because otherwise the native high-kcat enzyme drains the substrate before the heterologous step can act.
alternatives_considered: Knocking down IlvA - not attempted in this study

experiments.purpose: Determine which of six possible reaction orders (R1-R6) operate for IPDO production from leucine

experiments.conditions: FM-II + 5 mM precursor, 48 h; in vitro assays per Methods
experiments.control: Strain x precursor combinations act as mutual route tests; in vitro absence-of-enzyme conditions (Suppl. Fig. 16)
experiments.readout: IPDO titer (GC); in vitro enzyme activities
experiments.analysis: route feasibility inferred from titer + in vitro activity/absence of activity
experiments.outcome: R1 functional (374.1 mg/L from 4OH-Leu), R3 functional but weaker (19.2 mg/L from KIC); R2, R4, R5, R6 excluded by lack of enzyme activity on required intermediates; both routes co-exist from leucine with R1 dominant

experiments.purpose: Identify best hydroxylase and alpha-keto decarboxylase for IPDO production (Route 1)
experiments.intervention: Strains IP01-IP07 swapping decarboxylase (KDC/PDC/THI3) or hydroxylase (MFL/AVI/IDO/GOX/BPE); codon-optimized synthesized genes

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: systematic enzyme-variant swapping is an active engineering action whose screen outcome selected the chassis for all subsequent optimization.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Integrated screening of enzyme variants to identify the best-performing pathway configuration.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Platform demonstrated with initial enzyme set, but hydroxylase catalytic efficiency identified as determinant of titers (GriE substrate-efficiency vs titer correlation) and MFL activity known to be poor.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Screening readout is measured in vivo titers across strains.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Best enzyme combination was determined empirically by comparative screening; paper notes in vitro Kcat/Km did not correlate with in vivo titers, so the choice rests on screening results plus literature Km tie-breaker, not on a predictive mechanism.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: new overexpression construct built to relieve leucine-supply limitation identified in exp05.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor supply enhancement: feedback-resistant leucine operon boosts endogenous leucine pool.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: IP01 titer rose from 15.3 to 230.5 mg/L when 25 mM leucine was supplemented, showing native leucine supply limits IPDO production from glucose.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Trigger and outcome are measured titers and amino-acid concentrations.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Use of feedback-resistant leuA^fbrBCD follows established 2-keto-acid-based pathway practice (ref 32); the feedback-resistance mechanism is known but the choice is presented as adopting an established tool rather than deriving from this paper's own mechanistic finding.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When amino-acid-derived product synthesis in E. coli is limited by endogenous amino-acid supply (shown by large titer gain upon feeding), apply overexpression of the feedback-resistant biosynthetic operon (e.g., leuA^fbrBCD), because relieving feedback inhibition increases the precursor pool without chemical feeding.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: new construct pushing pyruvate->KIC flux; produced next lineage strain and revealed valine-shunt problem driving IP10 design.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor supply: acetolactate synthase + ketol-acid reductoisomerase/DAD enhance flux from pyruvate to KIC, the direct leucine precursor.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Leucine supply still limiting after leuA^fbrBCD (broth leucine only 0.22 mg/L); KIC is the direct leucine precursor.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titers (55.7 mg/L) and valine byproduct measurements.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: AlsS from B. subtilis explicitly adopted because a previous study (ref 33, Atsumi et al.) used it to increase cytoplasmic KIC supply.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When the amino-acid precursor pool is still limiting after operon overexpression in E. coli keto-acid-derived product pathways, apply alsS + ilvCD overexpression to enhance pyruvate-to-keto-acid flux, because this increases cytosolic supply of the direct keto-acid precursor (validated for KIC in the IPDO system).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: targeted overexpression to redirect KIC flux away from valine; outcome confirmed reduced byproduct and higher titer.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Blocking competing flux: TyrB converts KIC selectively to leucine while unable to aminate KIV to valine, channeling flux toward product precursor and away from byproduct.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: IP09 accumulated 7.08 mg/L valine (3.04-fold IP08) because KIC/KIV are shared precursors of leucine and valine, so enhanced KIC supply was partially shunted to valine.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Byproduct and titer changes are measured; TyrB substrate specificity is literature-documented (ref 34).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper gives explicit enzyme-specificity mechanism: TyrB promiscuously converts KIC->leucine but cannot convert KIV->valine, so its overexpression preferentially drains KIC toward leucine (also referencing ref 34).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When enhancing keto-acid precursor supply in E. coli creates byproduct flux into a parallel amino-acid pathway (KIC/KIV -> leucine/valine in IPDO production), apply overexpression of an aminotransferase selective for the desired keto-acid (TyrB: KIC but not KIV), because its substrate specificity redirects flux toward the product precursor while starving the byproduct branch.
alternatives_considered: Dynamic regulation of IlvE - proposed as future work, not implemented

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: initiation of an evolution/screening campaign is an engineering action; selected mutants fed directly into production-strain improvement (IP11).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Rate-limiting enzyme engineering: hydroxylation identified as rate-limiting step, so MFL activity was improved by directed evolution.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Hydroxylation is the rate-limiting step (R1 dominance traced to low MFL activity on KIC; literature reports MFL activity far from technically useful).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Mutant improvements are measured in vitro activities and in vivo titers.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Beneficial mutations arose from random EP-PCR mutagenesis and growth-coupled screening, not from rational design; the structural explanations (H138 helix, S98 loop plasticity) are post hoc modeling hypotheses explicitly flagged as needing verification.
alternatives_considered: Rational design - deferred because no MFL crystal structure exists; CASTing proposed as future work

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1-Q3 pass: medium/selection setup was actively optimized in this study (yeast enrichment, exponential-phase induction) after initial poor growth, changing screening feasibility.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Integrated screening: coupling hydroxylase activity to succinate-auxotroph growth enables colony-size selection.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Leucine hydroxylation by MFL is stoichiometrically coupled to alpha-KG->succinate oxidation, so succinate prototrophy reports hydroxylase activity; initial M9 selection conditions gave poor growth and small growth differential.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Growth curves (Fig. 6b, Suppl. Fig. 18) measured; auxotroph strain itself was a gift/background (ref 35) but its optimization as selection tool was done here.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Selection principle rests on explicit reaction stoichiometry: hydroxylation consumes alpha-KG and releases succinate, restoring growth of ΔsucAΔaceAΔputA auxotroph (concept from ref 35, adapted and optimized here).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When evolving Fe(II)/alpha-KG-dependent amino-acid hydroxylases in E. coli, apply growth-coupled selection in a succinate auxotroph (ΔsucAΔaceAΔputA) with enriched M9 and exponential-phase induction, because hydroxylation stoichiometrically co-produces succinate, linking enzyme activity to growth rate.
alternatives_considered: Plain M9 with lag-phase IPTG - rejected due to poor growth and heavy IPTG burden

interventions_ddr.name: Homology modeling and docking of MFL mutants

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: modeling/docking interpret mutant structure-function post hoc; authors themselves caution the loop models are unreliable (31.2% identity) and mutation effects need experimental verification; it drove no new construct in this paper.
